exception: The response includes its trajectory, so a criterion about something the model did -- opened a file, viewed a figure, ran a script, wrote an output -- has a target.

The Limited Exception: where listing every workspace value would be impractical, a supplementary criterion whose failure is captured by other self-contained criteria is not counted. The covering criteria are named; each must exist, be positive and carry no Not Self Contained finding of its own; the criterion must not carry the value the answer turns on.

A negative criterion naming a class of wrong claims is judged on its subject and on what puts a claim in the class, in its own words and the field's ordinary terms, not on an inventory of the class's members. A class fixed only by material the criterion does not identify is the defect.

A negative criterion naming a class of wrong claims and giving examples of its members -- (e.g. S03 at exactly 7.0) -- is self-contained: the examples show a grader what puts a claim in the class. A positive line still names its value.

A criterion that introduces an item and states what it is or does -- its function, its role, the reaction it catalyses -- is one thing, even where the name alone identifies the item; so is the name a file must carry or the unit a value is stated in. A further finding about the item that the response has to reach from the task's material stays a second part.
A negative criterion whose parts together describe one wrong claim has no part a response can satisfy on its own.
A criterion carrying both a Major and a Moderate bundle is counted once, as Major; the identifying-property and one-wrong-claim exceptions apply here too.
An opposite-polarity pair is exempt when the negative is a proven hallucination: the negative fired against the graded run.

A criterion checking a value or verdict in the response and one checking that the same value or verdict is carried into an output file are not overlap in either direction; only the carryover's weight is judged, by the weights reading.
A negative naming a particular wrong claim -- a distractor, a wrong figure, a wrong route -- is not the positive stated the other way round, whether or not it fired.
A criterion drawing a conclusion from two others is not contained in them; a single criterion introducing and specifying related requirements is not overlap.
Specific answers given as examples -- "e.g.", in parentheses, "such as" -- are allowed.

Where the task's data determines a single answer, naming it is not overfit, for as long as the ground truth's answer holds: an answer resting on an inaccurate statement makes the criterion copying it an Incorrect Criteria finding instead. Requiring all of a set the ground truth lists is completeness; requiring the model to read the evidence is never overfit.
A workspace supporting less than the ground truth asserts is a gap in the material, reported as one and not filed against the criterion.
Precision pinned the same way across every numeric criterion is the task's own convention.
Judged on the criterion's primary requirement, and acceptable where the prompt is deliberately open-ended.
Long, technical or domain-heavy wording is fine while it has one reading; a value in a parenthetical that agrees with the material is clean.

Judged against the task's material and a check that settles the fact, never against the ground truth taken as given: the ground truth is one of the files checked, and a criterion repeating an inaccurate statement of it is a factual error. The finding names that statement. A doubt no check can settle is a note and never counts.

An Incorrect Criteria finding counts only once three voters from different model families, each reading blind, all find its statement inaccurate. A statement that is not confirmed leaves the finding reported and not counted.
Before Incorrect Criteria, a more specific category is used.
A negative criterion covers the requirement it guards; a requirement a unit test asserts is covered.
A spot-checked group counts once, never per member or per column.
A hallucination annotation is a wrong claim the run actually made. The quoted claim must be in the run's answer; an anticipated trap the run never fell for is not a missing criterion.
Where a reason the rubric needs no such criterion can be stated, the requirement is covered. The requirement is quoted from the prompt.
A weight one step from the reviewer's own pricing is inside the band; each criterion is priced on its own content, never against a budget for the criteria covering one ask.
A value already checked by a +5 criterion may be carried into an artifact check at +3 without penalty.
A two-step weight error counts as a moderate issue in the overall total.

Counted only where the wrong answers the criterion names were taken from the run: its particulars appear in the graded run's answer. An escapable criterion not copied from the run is reported and never counted.
An escape another criterion penalises is covered, and not counted. The covering criterion must exist in the rubric.
Naming specific values is acceptable; a value or set the task's material settles is the class boundary.
Only a negative criterion can be a double negative.
